jurisdiction.name: Cambodia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Cambodia has no AI law. AI is steered through the 2021 Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework and the 2022 Digital Government Policy, which commits to an AI policy and AI standards, while a National AI Strategy 2025-2030 went to consultation in June 2025 but had not been adopted. The National Bank's January 2026 technology and cyber risk guidelines set requirements for AI and machine learning, including human verification of significant automated decisions and disclosure that chatbots are not human. A personal data protection law is still being drafted, and there is no data protection authority yet.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft National AI Strategy, the draft data protection law and planned AI ethics guidelines have no published official text and are listed as leads.

instruments.english_title: Cambodia Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021-2035
instruments.issuing_authority: Royal Government of Cambodia (prepared by the Supreme National Economic Council)
instruments.current_status: In force as Cambodia's 15-year umbrella digital policy (2021-2035), put into use on 10 May 2021 according to the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, with the cover of the official English version reading 'Prepared by the Supreme National Economic Council, May 2021'. It is not a dedicated AI strategy; a monitoring and evaluation framework was under technical consultation in August 2025, and the draft National AI Strategy 2025-2030 is listed under Leads.
instruments.summary: The Royal Government's long-term policy framework for building a digital economy and society through three phases (digital foundations, adoption, transformation) and five goals, including digital government and trust in digital systems. Its digital-government and data-driven-governance measures call for expanding the use of artificial intelligence, data science and big data to create digital services, and for investing in infrastructure and the use of AI in data-driven governance systems. Implementation is assigned to ministries and digital committees with monitoring plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Umbrella national digital policy; contains Cambodia's first government-level AI measures (AI in digital services and data-driven governance).

instruments.summary: Sets out how the Royal Government will build digital government by 2035 through ten strategies and action plans covering connectivity, digital governance, public-sector digital transformation, human capital and innovation. It commits the government to develop a policy and principles, standards, frameworks and mechanisms for leading technologies including artificial intelligence, and to develop technical standards for AI, big data, IoT and blockchain in line with international best practice, alongside a Law on Digital Government and rules on government data sharing. It also promotes innovation of public services using AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Government-wide digital government policy; commits to an AI promotion policy and AI standards and frames public-sector AI use.

instruments.official_title: Technology and Cyber Risk Management Guidelines
instruments.english_title: Technology and Cyber Risk Management Guidelines (TCRMG)
instruments.current_status: Issued January 2026 (cover date) and listed on the NBC Guidelines (IT policy) page; supersedes the Technology Risk Management Guidelines issued in 2019, which did not contain an AI section. Requirements are framed as 'compliance requirements' assessed in supervision, applied on a risk basis; no effective date stated. Only the English version was found on the NBC site.
instruments.summary: The NBC's supervisory guidelines for banks and financial institutions on technology and cyber risk. Section 6.4 requires institutions to periodically assess AI/ML systems for legal and policy compliance, conduct comprehensive AI risk assessments, apply privacy and security by design, validate data and models against bias, use AI ethically (human autonomy, harm prevention, fairness, non-discrimination, transparency, explainability) and ensure robustness and safety. Related sections require human verification of solely big-data-based decisions that significantly affect customers and a right to challenge them, and require chatbots to disclose to customers that they are not human and to offer escalation to staff.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI-specific supervisory requirements in Cambodia's financial sector.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read via pdftotext (introduction, sections 6.3 big data, 6.4 AI/ML, 6.8 chatbot); cover dated January 2026; listed on the NBC Guidelines page

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Cambodia were searched in Khmer and English, including the posts and telecommunications ministry's legal listings and policies, other ministries and regulators. No qualifying material was found for binding law, government AI governance, ethics, procurement, data privacy, sandboxes, readiness indexes, generative AI, drafts, international instruments or historical documents. The Royal Gazette has no searchable online portal. Not yet verified from the official text: bills before parliament, the draft National AI Strategy, the draft personal data protection law and planned AI governance guidelines, which remain leads.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. Royal Gazette has no searchable online portal; National Assembly and Senate bill pages not reached. Policies sourced to the Khmer PDFs on MPTC, checked against the official English versions on the same host. Draft AI Strategy distributed only by QR code. ESCAP-MISTI report held as a lead (UN publication). Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Searched MPTC Law & Regulations listing and web for AI laws, sub-decrees, prakas and AI provisions in other laws (Khmer and English): no AI law or AI provision in force found. The draft Law on Personal Data Protection (MPTC, consultation July 2025) has no official published text (lead). No deepfake/automated-decision statute found. Royal Gazette not searchable online; nac.org.kh / senate.gov.kh not reached.; Government: Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021-2035 and Digital Government Policy 2022-2035 recorded (AI measures); draft National AI Strategy 2025-2030 held as lead (consultation 2025, not adopted, text only via QR/third-party hosts); MPTC AI Promotion Strategy draft and National AI and Data Science Research Centre held as leads. MPTC AI training for civil servants (May-June 2026) is a training programme, not a guideline: no public-sector AI/GenAI guideline found. MPTC press release No. 970 PT (23 April 2025) on AI governance work read: planned Cambodian Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics held as lead.; Ministries: MPTC (above); MISTI (ESCAP co-report, lead; 2023 landscape report not online); MoEYS searched (no AI guidance published; UNESCO-supported GenAI ethical framework project unfinished); MEF, health, justice, labour, interior, defence: searched, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: National Bank of Cambodia: Technology and Cyber Risk Management Guidelines (Jan 2026) recorded with AI/ML, big-data decision and chatbot requirements. NBFSA, TRC, SERC, competition, cyber: searched, nothing AI-specific found. No data protection authority exists yet.. Not reached: Royal Gazette (no searchable online portal); National Assembly / Senate bill pages (not searched directly). Could not verify: Draft National AI Strategy text on an official host (distributed only via QR code); Draft Law on Personal Data Protection text; Current adoption status of the National AI Strategy after July 2026. binding-law, government-governance, ethics, procurement, data-privacy, sandbox, index-readiness, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (coverage_audit.no_material_found_note): The Royal Gazette has no searchable online portal and parliament's bill pages were not searched directly; the draft National AI Strategy, the draft personal data protection law and planned AI governance guidelines remain leads to check.

leads.title: យុទ្ធសាស្ត្រជាតិស្តីពីបញ្ញាសិប្បនិម្មិត ២០២៥-២០៣០ (សេចក្តីព្រាង)
leads.note: MPTC opened a public consultation on the draft on 1 June 2025 (until 20 June 2025) at https://mptc.gov.kh/en/2025/06/announcement-on-progress-of-preparing-and-opening-public-consultation-on-draft-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy/ ; the draft, concept note and feedback form were distributed only via a QR code (not present on the page), so no official-host full text could be read. The English consultation version (v5, June 2025, six strategic priorities incl. ethical and responsible AI) circulates only on third-party hosts. National workshop held 1 July 2025; still described as not yet adopted in mid-2026. Promote as national_strategy once adopted text is published on an official site (or as consultation_draft if MPTC posts the draft itself). MPTC press release No. 970 PT of 23 April 2025 (https://asset.cambodia.gov.kh/mptc/2025/04/20250424-PR-Key-AI-Work-Final.pdf, unofficial English translation) states that the Royal Government approved the work by Letter No. 316 SCN.AS of 5 March 2024 and MPTC set up a Working Group on AI and Data Science R&D on 5 April 2024.

No official full text of the draft found on MPTC or other government sites, and no adopted law found as of 2026-10-12. Record under data-privacy (and drafts) when the official text is published.

leads.title: Artificial Intelligence: Empowering Innovation, Ethics, and Inclusion in Cambodia
leads.english_title: Artificial Intelligence: Empowering Innovation, Ethics, and Inclusion in Cambodia (UN ESCAP-MISTI COPAI report)
leads.issuing_authority: United Nations ESCAP with the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation
leads.note: Hosted on the MISTI CDN (https://cdn.misti.gov.kh/documents/20260409081135T17VXSvZjhsH.pdf, read 2026-10-12) but it is a United Nations publication (copyright UN 2025, ESCAP/2-TR/48) whose views are the authors'; it assesses Cambodia's AI landscape and recommends inter alia a National AI Ethics Framework. Not recorded as a government instrument; lead decides whether it counts under index-readiness. MISTI's earlier 'AI Landscape in Cambodia: Current Status and Future Trends' (2023, ISBN 9789924600091) was not found online on an official site. The UNESCO/CADT AI Readiness Assessment (RAM) report launched 1 July 2025 is a UNESCO publication (not recorded).
